title: Chapter 3 Quiz 6
description: How a program reads data from the user and shows results.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Which instruction reads a value typed on the keyboard?
questions.explanation: READ or INPUT retrieves a value from an input device.

questions.question: Which instruction shows a value on the screen?
questions.explanation: WRITE or DISPLAY sends a value to the output device.

questions.question: Which of these are **input** instructions?
questions.explanation: READ and INPUT bring data in. WRITE and DISPLAY send data out.

questions.question: What can the value of a WRITE or DISPLAY instruction be?
questions.explanation: It can be an identifier, a constant, an expression or a string.

questions.question: READ(grade1, grade2) reads two values.
questions.explanation: Several identifiers can be read in one instruction.

questions.question: The identifier used in READ must be declared before.
questions.explanation: The identifier must be an object previously declared in the VAR section.

questions.question: Put these lines in a sensible order to read two grades and show their average.
items: Declare Grade1, Grade2, Avg As Real
questions.explanation: Declare first, read the data, calculate, then display.

questions.question: Grade1 = 12 and Grade2 = 15. What does Avg ← (Grade1 + Grade2) / 2 give?
Complete the algorithm that reads a name and greets the user.
questions.explanation: READ takes the name in; WRITE sends the greeting out.
